operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are plain ASCII, no spaces/mixed case; still double-quote in generated SQL per spec.
Tiny DB: Services=4, Participants=15, Events=15, Participants_in_Events=18 rows; original read is trivial, no sampling needed.
All declared types dispatch cleanly: INTEGER->Number, CHAR(15)/VARCHAR(255)->String; no crash-fallback, no Date/Time/Bool/Bit columns.
No text-stored dates, no NULLs anywhere (null_rate 0.0 on every column), no storage-class/declared-type contradictions (integer->INTEGER, text->CHAR/VARCHAR).

FKs: Events.Service_ID->Services.Service_ID (parent unique PK, exists); Participants_in_Events.Event_ID->Events.Event_ID and .Participant_ID->Participants.Participant_ID (both parents exist, unique PKs). No dangling FKs, no self-references.
Composite PK on Participants_in_Events (Event_ID, Participant_ID) -> composite-PK member max_l0=30 path in 3.3.
Single-column PKs on Services, Participants, Events -> max_l0=inf path.
No UNIQUE/CHECK constraints in DDL; 'unique'/'check' line scan finds nothing.
No views, triggers, or extra indexes in DDL.
Table order: Services, Participants (level 0) -> Events (level 1) -> Participants_in_Events (level 2); no cycles.
Service_Type_Code and Participant_Type_Code are low-cardinality (4 and 2 distinct) but declared CHAR(15) -> String fuzzer, not ENUM.
Event_Details has only 2 distinct values ('Success','Fail') but VARCHAR(255) -> String fuzzer.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all *_ID columns: uniform in [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] for INTEGER (scale=0), then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> mostly small ints, rarely matching original IDs (2,5,6,8,...).

String fuzzer on Service_Type_Code/Participant_Type_Code/Event_Details/Participant_Details: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20 (or 0..15/0..255 from args), plus 5 sampled originals, plus contaminate suffix/prefix/drop.
FK columns (Events.Service_ID, Participants_in_Events.Event_ID/Participant_ID) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> ties/duplicates in child, plausible joins.
PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) keeps first occurrence; composite PK on Participants_in_Events drops many rows since Event_ID and Participant_ID are drawn independently from small parent sets.
Table sizes: rand_lin gives 30+int(u*200) ~ 30..230 rows per table, or level-based 1+30u, x4 per level capped 2500 -> Services/Participants small, Participants_in_Events potentially large.

Likely FN driver: Number fuzzer produces IDs in [-1,1] that never match original small-int IDs (2,5,6,8,26,66,...), so equality/join predicates on IDs rarely hit; also String fuzzer produces implausible type codes ('aB3()') that never equal 'Marriage'/'Organizer'.

Likely FP driver: FK consistency creates many-to-one ties (Events.Service_ID duplicates) and composite-PK dedup leaves sparse Participants_in_Events, so COUNT/DISTINCT/join-cardinality queries can accidentally match or mismatch.

Low-cardinality columns (Participant_Type_Code 2 distinct, Event_Details 2 distinct) get random strings that never reproduce the 2-value domain -> GROUP BY on these yields many singleton groups, unlike original.
Participant_Details (names) gets random strings, not name-like -> LIKE '%Batz%' style predicates never match.

No NULLs in original, but String/Number fuzzers can emit NULL only via FK-empty-parent path (won't happen here since parents non-empty) -> NOT NULL constraints rarely violated, so few insert failures.
p=0.2 default with 0.3 chance of p=0 per instance: some instances are pure-element (original-value) sampling, others mostly fresh.
